title: Ten-Step Restoration Sprint & Shadow Mentoring Handbook
author: Priya Nair
content:
Overview

Purpose: This handbook describes a focused, repeatable Ten-Step Restoration Sprint used during multi-system outages and pairs that operational flow with a structured shadow-mentor program to accelerate oncall proficiency. It is intended for first responders, bridge operators, service owners, and SRE mentors.

Scope: Applies to production incidents that meet SLO-impacting criteria (see SLO thresholds section). Not intended for low-severity config errors or scheduled maintenance.

Owner: Eng SRE team. Primary contact: oncall-lead@redwood.example.com.

Quick links: runbook library, status page templates, postmortem template, incident evidence checklist.

Audience and roles

- Incident Initiator: the first person to acknowledge the alert and call the bridge.
- Bridge Operator: facilitates the incident bridge, coordinates comms, and enforces the Ten-Step Sprint cadence.
- Primary Resolver: service owner(s) leading technical work for the impacted service(s).
- Secondary Resolvers: cross-functional engineers called in to assist (networking, infra, runtime).
- Shadow: junior responder who observes and documents actions during the sprint.
- Mentor: senior SRE who leads post-incident coaching and retro facilitation.

How to use this document

- Use the numbered Ten-Step Sprint for initial restoration (first 60–90 minutes).
- Run the shadow mentoring checklist in parallel to create training artefacts.
- After containment, follow the Post-Incident Evidence & Draft Postmortem template included below.

SLO thresholds that trigger Ten-Step Sprint

| Severity | Symptom | SLO impact | Trigger |
|---------|---------|------------|---------|
| Sev1 | Total region outage for hosted API | >= 99.5% reduction in success rate for 5+ minutes | Auto-trigger after 3x alert flood or manual bridge |
| Sev2 | Significant latency increase | > 200ms p95 increase across customer requests for 15+ minutes | Review/bridge by oncall |

Ten-Step Restoration Sprint (primary runbook)

1) Acknowledge & Bridge (0–5m)
   - Incident Initiator: acknowledge the alert in PagerDuty and create a bridge (Zoom/Google Meet).
   - Bridge Operator: open the incident channel (#inc-xxxx) and post initial status: impacted services, region, estimated blast radius, primary contact.
   - Shadow: note timestamps, alert IDs, and initial metrics snapshot.

2) Quick Impact Triage (5–10m)
   - Primary Resolver: confirm service(s) affected using dashboards (console/model-serving, ingress, and edge metrics).
   - Bridge: classify impact (regional vs. global, data plane vs. control plane).
   - Output: short impact statement to stakeholders.

3) Stabilize Traffic (10–20m)
   - If applicable, apply graduated traffic control: rate-limits, scaled back routing policies, or traffic-division to healthy regions.
   - Use fallback model variants or reduced sequence length mode where supported to temporarily reduce CPU/GPU pressure.

4) Hotfix Window (20–40m)
   - Primary Resolver and Secondary Resolvers: run validated mitigation steps from specific service runbooks (see related runbook IDs).
   - Keep changes small, reversible, and documented in the incident channel.

5) Validate Restoration (30–50m)
   - Run synthetic probes against restored endpoints. Confirm p95/p99 latency and error-rate trends returning to baseline.
   - Shadow: capture pre/post metric snapshots and the commands used.

6) Customer Status & Tiered Notifications (immediately after validation)
   - Bridge Operator: publish customer-facing status update using the template below.
   - For enterprise customers impacted by the incident, trigger account-level outreach per the escalation matrix.

7) Stabilization Monitoring (50–90m)
   - Maintain increased sampling and tracing for 3x normal volume for 90 minutes.
   - Set temporary alerts at tighter thresholds (e.g., 50% of SLO slack) to catch reversion.

8) Evidence Collection & Triage for Postmortem (start while stabilizing)
   - Collect logs, traces, config diffs, rollout metadata, and full command history. Attach artifacts to the incident ticket.
   - Shadow: curate a short evidence index with direct links.

9) Restore Normal Ops & Runbook Handover (90–120m)
   - Roll back temporary mitigations and revert traffic controls when confident.
   - Primary Resolver: schedule a 60-minute triage deep-dive with the mentor and product owner within 48 hours.

10) Close Bridge & Draft Postmortem (post sprint)
   - Bridge Operator: move the channel to read-only and create a draft postmortem using the included template.
   - Mentor: assign action owners with clear SLAs for mitigation items.

Shadow-Mentor Program (parallel process)

Purpose: Turn incidents into repeatable learning opportunities and accelerate new responder ramp.

Shadow checklist (during sprint):
- Record timestamps for each decision and action.
- Note who is contacted and the exact commands or consoles used.
- Capture any runbook gaps or ambiguous steps.
- Collect a short list of 3 teachable moments for the retro.

Mentor responsibilities (post sprint):
- Within 48 hours: review the evidence index and draft postmortem with the shadow.
- Within 7 days: run a 30–60 minute learning session with the wider oncall rota covering the teachable moments and suggested runbook updates.
- Ensure at least one runbook edit or clarification is merged per incident for which the shadow prepared artifacts.

Escalation matrix (quick reference)

- Local service issue -> Primary Resolver -> Service Lead (15 min)
- Cross-service or infra -> Add Secondary Resolver(s) + SRE oncall (10 min)
- Prolonged SLO loss > 1 hour -> Paging to Eng Director + Product Ops (escalate at 60m)
- Customer-impacting > 4 hours -> Executive status + CS/AE briefing (escalate at 4h)

Status Page & Customer Comms Templates

Public status template (to be posted on status.redwood.example.com):
- Title: Incident - {service} - {brief cause} (Region)
- Impact: Short sentence (e.g., "Customers in us-west experienced elevated errors and increased latency between 12:03–12:45 UTC.")
- Current status: Investigating / Identified / Mitigating / Restored / Monitoring
- Next update: {time + 30m}
- Notes: High-level mitigation steps and workarounds.

Enterprise account brief (email/Slack DM):
- Subject: Incident update — {service} — {short impact statement}
- Body: One-sentence impact, actions taken, ETA for more info, contact person (SRE lead and AM), apologies and credit guidance (if applicable).

Post-Incident Evidence & Draft Postmortem Template

1) Summary (1–3 sentences): What happened and visible customer impact.
2) Timeline: concise, timestamped actions (use ISO-8601).
3) Root cause hypothesis / final root cause: technical summary.
4) Contributing factors: people, process, tooling, and telemetry gaps.
5) Mitigation and long-term fixes: owner and ETA.
6) Customer impact and remediation: crediting plan, customer comms sent.
7) Evidence index: links to logs, traces, recordings, rollout IDs, and config diffs.
8) Retrospective notes and teachable moments.

Runbook governance and ownership

- Each service runbook must list a primary owner, secondary owner, and last-tested date.
- Runbooks must include safe roll-forward and roll-back commands and a quick-impact checklist.
- Runbook review cadence: quarterly for high-risk services, bi-annual for others.

Game-day & Mentored Simulation schedule

- Quarterly Game-Days: 3 planned scenarios per quarter (network partition, kv-cache storm, auth tier regression). At least one scenario must use the shadow-mentor pairing.
- Shadow simulations: monthly 60-minute labs where a shadow leads a mini-restoration and a mentor grades the artifacts produced.

Metrics and KPIs to track program health

- Mean Time To Restore (MTTR) — target: reduce by 20% year-over-year.
- Shadow ramp time — % of shadows qualified to be solo oncall within 4 months.
- Runbook churn — number of runbook edits per incident (target: >=1 edit/incident).
- Postmortem completion rate — 100% for Sev1/Sev2 within 7 days.

Appendices

A. Evidence collection checklist (CLI commands and dashboards)
- curl and synthetic probe examples, steps to download logs from logging cluster, query examples for traces, recommended span sampling rates.

B. Restorative CLI snippets (examples with placeholders)
- Rollout rollback: 
  gcloud run services update-traffic SERVICE --to-revisions REVISION --region REGION
- Temporary rate-limit (kong example):
  curl -X POST https://api-gateway/config -d '{"limit":100}'

C. Customer status example (realistic copy)
- \"12:10 UTC — We are investigating increased error rates for text-generation in us-west. Our mitigation is to route new requests to our fallback model variant which reduces throughput but restores successful responses. Next update: 12:40 UTC.\"

D. Learning outcomes rubric for mentors
- Level 1: Shadow can summarize timeline and reproduce evidence index without guidance.
- Level 2: Shadow can perform 30% of mitigation steps under supervision.
- Level 3: Shadow can lead a mini-sprint with a mentor ready to intervene.
